translationRepairs: He was soon reappointed vice director and ordered to escort the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu from Baringol to Ili and to oversee the pastures of Pacification Deputy General-in-Chief Sarlar.
He was soon reappointed vice director and ordered to escort the Jilong Khutuktu from Baringol to Ili and to oversee the pastures of Pacification Deputy General-in-Chief Sarlar.
s0075 has 濟隆呼圖克圖, the Jilong Khutuktu; Jebtsundamba would require 哲布尊丹巴 and is a different lineage. The rest of the sentence (reappointment, Baringol to Ili, Sarlar’s pastures) is already accurate.

Shortly afterward he was again appointed vice director and ordered to escort the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu from Baringol to Ili and to supervise the pastures of Pacification Deputy General-in-Chief Sarlar.
Shortly afterward he was again appointed vice director and ordered to escort the Jilong Khutuktu from Baringol to Ili and to supervise the pastures of Pacification Deputy General-in-Chief Sarlar.
The literal field likewise misidentifies 濟隆呼圖克圖 as Jebtsundamba; Jilong Khutuktu restores the correct reading without altering the surrounding accurate phrasing.
His grandson Sun {Shu} inherited the hereditary rank and rose to commander of the Dengzhou garrison in Shandong.
His grandson Shu inherited the hereditary rank and rose to commander of the Dengzhou garrison in Shandong.
s0175 opens 孫{澍}: 孫 is the kinship term ‘grandson’, not the surname Sun, and the personal name is 澍 (Shu). Removing the invented surname leaves an accurate inheritance and Dengzhou appointment.
His grandson Sun {Shu} inherited the hereditary office and rose to be commander of the Dengzhou garrison in Shandong.
His grandson Shu inherited the hereditary office and rose to be commander of the Dengzhou garrison in Shandong.
The literal repeats the same error: 孫 is ‘grandson’ and the given name is 澍; ‘His grandson Shu’ matches the Chinese without inventing a surname Sun.
